3. GAME, REVENUE AND THE USD 1,000,000 THRESHOLD

A "Game" is a video game or interactive entertainment product whose runtime
incorporates Ignis or a modification of it. Ports, storefront versions, editions,
downloadable content and expansions of substantially the same Game are one
Game. Genuinely independent sequels are separate Games. Do not split a Game
between entities, stores or platforms to avoid the threshold. Sales of unrelated
games and general company revenue do not count against a Game's threshold.

"Game Revenue" is worldwide revenue attributable to that Game, including game
sales, paid access, attributable subscriptions, in-game purchases, DLC and
advertising. Include amounts received by a store, publisher or related party
on Your behalf before their commissions. Allocate bundle/subscription proceeds
reasonably and consistently to the Game. Product advances and minimum guarantees
count once, without counting the same recouped proceeds twice. Exclude genuine
loans, equity investment, grants without product entitlements, voluntary gifts
without product entitlements, and sales taxes/VAT collected for a government.
Refunds and chargebacks reduce revenue once, not again as expenses.

The first USD 1,000,000 of cumulative Game Revenue is exempt. No royalty is
payable for a Game that has not exceeded that amount. The threshold does not
reset annually or per platform. Crossing it does not create a retroactive
royalty on exempt revenue or on the profit earned from that exempt revenue.
Standalone art, video or other independent output that does not incorporate
Ignis at runtime does not become royalty-bearing solely because Ignis helped
create it. No royalty under this License applies to non-Game uses.

4. PROFIT, ELIGIBLE COSTS AND LOSSES

The royalty is 1% (one percent) of Eligible Profit, NOT a percentage of revenue,
not a percentage of Your company's profit and not a fee per installation.

Eligible Costs are actual, documented, reasonable costs attributable to the Game:
development and contractor costs, salaries and employer charges for work on the
Game, production, licensing of game content, publishing/distribution commissions,
store and payment fees, marketing, hosting, operation, maintenance, customer
support, and taxes actually borne and attributable to the Game. Allocate shared
costs and capital assets reasonably, consistently and without duplicate expense
or depreciation deductions. Related-party charges and owner remuneration must
reflect actual services at reasonable market rates.

Do not deduct unrelated business costs, dividends, distributions to owners,
loan principal, notional unpaid labor, speculative future costs, fines, this
royalty itself, or an amount already deducted elsewhere. Do not count a refund,
tax exclusion, publisher recoupment or other cost twice. Keep consistent records
of receipts and costs. Foreign currency amounts must use a reasonable,
consistently applied published exchange-rate source; record the source and dates.

Calculate the remaining unrecovered Game loss at the threshold ("Opening Loss")
after applying exempt revenue to the eligible costs allocated to that revenue.
Pre-threshold profit is exempt; pre-threshold unrecovered costs remain recoverable.
Keep a cumulative balance of post-threshold revenue (R), eligible costs allocated
to that post-threshold revenue (C), and Opening Loss (L):

    Eligible Profit = max(0, R - C - L)
    Cumulative Royalty = 0.01 * Eligible Profit
    Current Payment = max(0, Cumulative Royalty - royalties already paid)

If You cross the threshold during a calendar quarter, split that quarter's
revenue at the remaining exemption. Use reliable contemporaneous records to
allocate that quarter's costs between the exempt and post-threshold portions;
otherwise allocate them in the same proportion as that quarter's revenue. Apply
the same method consistently. Costs from earlier quarters and the exempt part
of the crossing quarter determine Opening Loss. Later quarters are entirely
post-threshold. Record the calculation and avoid double recovery of costs.

Losses carry forward for that Game. If later losses reduce the cumulative
royalty below amounts already paid, the excess is a credit against future
royalties for the same Game; no cash refund is required except to correct an
accounting error or where mandatory law requires it. There is no minimum royalty.

5. REPORTING, PAYMENT AND VERIFICATION

Within 60 days after the first calendar quarter in which the Game exceeds the
threshold, privately notify Licensor and provide a royalty report. Thereafter,
provide a report and pay the amount due within 60 days after each calendar
quarter while the Game earns revenue or has a payment due. Reports may show
zero profit and zero payment. Before the threshold, no routine report or product
registration is required, but keep records supporting the exemption.

A report identifies the Game and responsible business, reporting period,
cumulative revenue, remaining exemption, post-threshold revenue, categories of
eligible costs, Opening Loss, carried losses/credits, Eligible Profit, prior
payments, exchange rates and amount due. Use aggregate figures; do not disclose
players' personal data. Submit reports through a private channel agreed with
Licensor, never in a public issue, repository or discussion.

Request secure private reporting/payment instructions through the maintainer
contact route on the project profile. Payment is in USD by an agreed lawful
method. If You timely request instructions and Licensor does not provide them,
payment is deferred without penalty until 15 days after they are supplied;
retain the report and funds due. The obligation is not forgiven. No bank account
or payment recipient change in a public issue alone is a valid instruction.

Retain supporting records for five years after the relevant report. At most
once per calendar year, Licensor may request a proportionate review by an
independent accountant under confidentiality, with at least 30 days' notice,
limited to the records needed for this Game and calculation. Licensor pays the
review cost, unless it establishes an underpayment exceeding both 5% of the
amount due for the reviewed period and USD 1,000; in that case You reimburse
reasonable documented review costs and the underpayment. Correct errors promptly.
Confidential reports may be used only for administration, verification and legal
enforcement of this License, or disclosure required by law.
